title: The owner's empire collapses
summary: The Bears' financial backer's company went into receivership in late 1989; in the 1990 pre-season players threatened to strike, the AFL took the club over and resold it to a Gold Coast businessman.
penalty_or_outcome: Club survived under a new private owner, who later handed it back to a member-based structure.
game_hook: Unpaid wages: morale falls; coach chooses to back the players' strike threat (morale up, board and league down) or side with the league.

title: The VFL becomes the AFL
summary: The Victorian Football League renamed itself the Australian Football League before the 1990 season, signalling a national competition.
game_hook: Era opener news story; board starts talking about national rivals and interstate recruiting.

title: Save Our Skins
summary: Richmond had to raise $1 million by 31 October 1990 or fold; supporters rattled tins, held an MCG rally and a legends match.
penalty_or_outcome: Club survived (sources say just over $1m raised); debt lingered for two decades (about $6m still in 2011).
game_hook: Broke club: board cuts the football budget; coach can front fundraisers (members, press) and must play kids instead of recruiting.

title: Port's secret deal and the birth of the Crows
summary: Port Adelaide signed a heads of agreement with the AFL in July 1990; Glenelg and other SANFL clubs won a Supreme Court injunction, and the SANFL formed the Adelaide Crows, who entered in 1991.
penalty_or_outcome: Port blocked until 1997; Adelaide admitted for 1991.
game_hook: New rival in 1991; South Australian players on your list may ask to go home.

title: Bears players threaten to strike
summary: Part of the Bears' 1990 ownership crisis: players threatened strike action during the pre-season before the AFL stepped in.
game_hook: Merged into the Bears collapse event if both fire; listed so a 1990 start can show it alone.

title: Farewell to Windy Hill
summary: Essendon played its last home-and-away games at Windy Hill in 1991 and took its home games to the MCG from 1992.
penalty_or_outcome: Bigger crowds and gate takings; suburban home edge lost.
game_hook: Board proposes the move: more money versus losing the small-ground home advantage.

title: Swans on the brink
summary: After winning 15 games across 1990-92 under failing private ownership, the club told the AFL it could not go on; the clubs waived about $1.95m in licence fees, gave three years of working capital and priority picks, and in 1993 the club returned to member ownership.
penalty_or_outcome: Licence fee waived, working capital, priority draft picks; a 26-game losing streak ended in 1993.
game_hook: Bailout with strings: priority picks and cash in exchange for league control; coach inherits a gutted list.

title: Moorabbin's last AFL game
summary: St Kilda stopped playing home games at Moorabbin after 1992 and moved them to Waverley Park.
game_hook: Ground-move news story; small home-ground morale bonus ends.

title: Racial abuse at Victoria Park
summary: After St Kilda won at Victoria Park in April 1993, an Indigenous St Kilda player answered racist abuse from the crowd by lifting his jumper and pointing to his skin.
penalty_or_outcome: No club penalty; the image built pressure that led to Rule 30 in 1995.
game_hook: Press conference: coach is asked about crowd abuse of his player; the answer moves that player's morale and press relations.

title: The final eight
summary: The AFL went from a final six to a final eight in 1994, with the first week drawn 1 v 8, 2 v 7, 3 v 6 and 4 v 5.
penalty_or_outcome: Rule change; the system ran until 1999.
game_hook: News story; the board's finals target can rise from top six to top eight, and a middling list now has a real shot at September.

title: Fitzroy moves to the Western Oval
summary: Broke and without a ground of its own, Fitzroy left Princes Park for a better ground-sharing deal at Footscray's Western Oval from 1994.
penalty_or_outcome: Ground-sharing lease at the Western Oval, 1994-1996.
game_hook: Cash-strapped club gets a better ground deal elsewhere: money versus members, training base and home advantage.

title: The Melbourne Lions that never were
summary: In late July 1994 Melbourne and Fitzroy reached an in-principle deal to merge as the Melbourne Lions for 1995, and the AFL Commission backed it; Fitzroy insisted its name stay, and the Melbourne board walked away.
penalty_or_outcome: No merger; Fitzroy kept looking for a partner until 1996.
game_hook: Merger approach from a struggling club: the board asks the coach whether the extra players are worth the name, the members and the jumper.

title: Rule 30: the vilification rule
summary: After an Essendon Indigenous player complained of racial abuse by an opponent in the 1995 Anzac Day match and the mediation was seen to fail, the AFL brought in its racial and religious vilification rule later in 1995.
penalty_or_outcome: New rule: vilification becomes a reportable offence.
game_hook: League rule event; from here a vilification report can cost a club a player through suspension.

title: Fremantle joins
summary: Fremantle entered the AFL in 1995 as Western Australia's second club.
game_hook: New rival bids for WA-born players on your list.

title: The Bombers' 1990s cap breaches
summary: A league and tax office investigation found Essendon breached the salary cap and draft rules between about 1991 and 1996.
penalty_or_outcome: Sources differ: roughly $600,000-$638,250 in fines and back tax (part suspended) and exclusion from early national draft rounds plus the pre-season and rookie drafts. Announcement year UNCERTAIN (late 1990s).
game_hook: Board asks the coach to keep quiet about side payments; if exposed, lose picks and pay the fine.

title: Players' strike threat (mid-1990s)
summary: A labour history account says mid-1990s strikes over injury compensation and the players' share of revenue were averted when clubs met some demands. UNCERTAIN: single source, no exact year.
game_hook: Use only after a better source: pay dispute, morale versus board.

title: Fitzroy's end
summary: Fitzroy's creditor appointed an administrator in June 1996; a near-agreed merger with North Melbourne was voted down by club presidents and the AFL steered Fitzroy into the Brisbane Bears, who became the Brisbane Lions for 1997.
penalty_or_outcome: Fitzroy left the AFL after 1996; the merged club took a group of Fitzroy players (number UNCERTAIN, commonly given as eight) and Fitzroy's heritage.
game_hook: Director ruling: always happens unless the club is a regular finalist (then a slim chance anyway); a struggling club gets no choice. Lists merge, protected players chosen, morale shock.

title: The Melbourne Hawks vote
summary: The AFL backed a Melbourne-Hawthorn merger; on 16 September 1996 Melbourne members narrowly voted yes (4679-4229) but Hawthorn members voted no (5241-2841), killing it.
penalty_or_outcome: No merger; Hawthorn membership more than doubled the next year.
game_hook: Members' vote: the coach's public stance sways it; if merged, two lists combine; if rejected, a membership boost.

title: The merger game
summary: The round 22, 1996 Melbourne v Hawthorn match was played under the merger cloud with 'No Merger' signs throughout the crowd.
game_hook: Pre-match story: the club resisting the merger gets a morale lift from the crowd.

title: Port Adelaide and the Lions enter
summary: Port Adelaide joined the AFL in 1997, the same year the merged Brisbane Lions began; Port was barred from its prison-bars jumper after Collingwood objected.
game_hook: New rival; SA players; jumper row is press flavour only.

title: Western Oval farewell
summary: The Western Bulldogs played their last AFL home game at the Western Oval in 1997.
penalty_or_outcome: Home games moved to bigger grounds.
game_hook: Ground-move news story.

clubs: West Coast; Geelong; Collingwood; Hawthorn; Richmond; Western Bulldogs
title: The 1998 cap sweep
summary: An AFL investigation in 1998 found six clubs over the salary cap: West Coast by $165,000 across 1997-98, Geelong by $154,000 in 1997, and four others by smaller amounts. UNCERTAIN: every figure traces back to one list (Wikipedia and copies of it).
penalty_or_outcome: West Coast fined $100,000 and lost its third-round pick; Geelong fined $77,000; Collingwood $47,500; Hawthorn $45,000; Richmond $21,000; Bulldogs $5,300. Geelong, Collingwood and Richmond were barred from the 1999 pre-season draft.
game_hook: League audit: a club a little over the cap pays a fine and loses a late pick or pre-season draft access; the board asks the coach which contract to trim.

title: Coach out after a 71-point loss
summary: Brisbane sacked its coach after a 71-point loss to Fremantle in round 11 of 1998, with eight rounds left; an assistant took over as caretaker.
penalty_or_outcome: Caretaker for the rest of 1998; the club took the wooden spoon, then hired a premiership coach.
game_hook: Board patience event: a 71-point loss and a 2-9 record end the coach's run mid-season.

title: A new president with a new ticket
summary: On 29 October 1998 a high-profile TV personality took over as Collingwood president, bringing a new board ticket in at an extraordinary general meeting; members changed the constitution so two of his allies could sit on the board.
penalty_or_outcome: Board clean-out; he stayed president until 2021.
game_hook: New president arrives with big plans: more money and press attention, higher board expectations, and a coach who has to win him over.

title: The Demons confess
summary: Melbourne's president volunteered information about salary cap breaches of about $810,000 from 1995 to 1998.
penalty_or_outcome: About $600,000 fine ($250,000 suspended in one source); 1999 first-round pick (No. 5) went to Fremantle; excluded from early draft rounds and the 1999 pre-season draft (scope UNCERTAIN).
game_hook: Self-report choice: confess for a lighter penalty or risk being caught later for a heavier one.

title: Victoria Park farewell
summary: Collingwood played its last AFL home game at Victoria Park in 1999.
penalty_or_outcome: Home games moved to the MCG and later Docklands.
game_hook: Ground-move news story.

title: Waverley Park closes
summary: The AFL played its last match at Waverley Park in 1999 and later sold the ground; its tenants moved to the new Docklands stadium.
game_hook: Ground-move news story for Waverley tenants.

title: The Kangaroos
summary: North Melbourne played as the Kangaroos from 1999 to 2007 and took some home games interstate (Sydney around 1999-2002, Carrara in 2007; years UNCERTAIN).
game_hook: Board sells home games interstate: money versus home advantage and member anger.

title: Colonial Stadium opens
summary: The roofed Docklands stadium opened in 2000 as Colonial Stadium; its early playing surface drew heavy criticism.
game_hook: News story; early-years surface could raise injury talk (flavour).

title: Hawthorn heads to Tasmania
summary: Hawthorn began playing home games at York Park, Launceston, in 2001 under a Tasmanian government deal.
game_hook: Board offers sold home games: money versus travel and home advantage.

title: Seven loses the footy
summary: A News Limited consortium with Nine, Ten and Foxtel won the 2002-2006 broadcast rights, ending Seven's long run.
game_hook: News story; distribution money changes club budgets.

title: Brown paper bags
summary: Carlton paid four players outside the salary cap in 2000-2001, reportedly some in cash in brown paper bags through a third-party businessman.
penalty_or_outcome: Record fine ($930,000 or $987,500 depending on source); lost priority picks Nos. 1 and 2 in 2002 and first and second round picks in 2003 (some sources also 2004); out of the 2003 pre-season draft; directors removed at the 2002 board election. Carlton took its first wooden spoon that year.
game_hook: Board offers secret third-party payments to keep a star: accept (risk losing top picks) or refuse (he leaves).

title: Colonial becomes Telstra Dome
summary: The Docklands stadium was renamed Telstra Dome in 2002.
game_hook: Short news story.

title: A small cap breach
summary: Essendon exceeded the 2002 salary cap by about $106,000.
game_hook: Light version of the cap event for any club over the cap.

title: Promised a flag, gone by round 17
summary: Hawthorn's coach said in the pre-season the Hawks would win the premiership; by July they were second last, he said he would go at season's end, and after an 80-point loss in round 17 he left at once.
penalty_or_outcome: Caretaker for the rest of 2004 (sources split on sacked or resigned); a new coach was appointed for 2005.
game_hook: Press conference trap: a bold pre-season promise sets the board's bar; miss it badly and the board stops waiting.

title: A home game in Darwin
summary: The Bulldogs took a home game to Darwin's Marrara Oval each year from 2004, starting with round 20 against Port Adelaide, the ground's first premiership match.
penalty_or_outcome: Sold home game each year (about 2004-2008); the first drew 13,271 and Port won by 86 points.
game_hook: Board sells a home game to the Top End: money versus travel, heat and home advantage.

title: Three-strikes drugs policy
summary: The AFL and players introduced an illicit drugs policy in 2005: confidential testing, a player named only on a third strike.
penalty_or_outcome: Policy; criticised for secrecy; tightened to two strikes around 2015-16 (sources differ).
game_hook: League news; press asks coaches about drug culture.

title: Princes Park farewell
summary: Carlton played its last AFL home match at Princes Park in 2005.
penalty_or_outcome: Home games moved to the MCG and Docklands.
game_hook: Ground-move news story.

title: Sirengate
summary: St Kilda and Fremantle drew in round 5 of 2006 in Launceston, but the umpires had not heard the final siren and St Kilda's last behind came after it; the AFL Commission struck out that behind and gave Fremantle the win.
penalty_or_outcome: Result changed from a draw to a Fremantle win (four premiership points), only the second result ever changed on protest.
game_hook: Disputed finish: the club can lodge a protest (board and press pressure, a chance at the points) or let it go.

title: Seven and Ten win the footy back
summary: In January 2006 Seven and Ten used their first-and-last rights to match Nine's $780 million offer for the 2007-2011 free-to-air rights; Seven also dropped its court fight with Ten.
penalty_or_outcome: $780 million over five years, $87.5 million of it in kind; the pay-TV part was still unsettled in August 2006.
game_hook: News story; bigger TV money lifts every club's distribution from 2007 and the board loosens the football budget.

title: Coach out after the elimination final
summary: Days after losing the 2006 elimination final, St Kilda announced its coach was gone, calling it a mutual agreement; reports said the board doubted he could win a flag and wanted him to loosen his grip on the football department.
penalty_or_outcome: Coaching change in September 2006 (sacked or mutual, sources differ).
game_hook: Board review after a finals exit: hand over control of the football department or risk the sack.

title: Drug culture at the premier
summary: A year after its 2006 flag, West Coast sacked and delisted a former captain over drug-related conduct; an AFL-ordered report found the club had shut its eyes to a drug culture by 2003.
penalty_or_outcome: Player's contract torn up; AFL 12-month ban for disrepute; no club fine found.
game_hook: Board demands a culture purge: sack a star (talent loss) or protect him (press and board fallout).

title: No to the Gold Coast
summary: The AFL wanted the Kangaroos to relocate to the Gold Coast; on 6 December 2007 the board rejected the move to a standing ovation from members.
penalty_or_outcome: Stayed in Melbourne; the Gold Coast got a new club in 2011.
game_hook: Relocation offer: money and security versus members and identity; the coach's voice sways the board.

title: Debt demolition
summary: Melbourne, heavily in debt, launched a fundraising drive under a new president in 2008.
game_hook: Broke-club event: tight football budget; coach fronts fundraising.

title: Telstra Dome becomes Etihad Stadium
summary: The Docklands stadium was renamed Etihad Stadium in 2009.
game_hook: Short news story.

title: The succession plan
summary: In 2009 Collingwood announced its premiership coach would hand over to a former captain after 2011; it ended in an awkward exit after the 2011 grand final loss.
game_hook: Board proposes naming your successor: stability versus a lame-duck coach.

title: The drawn grand final
summary: The 2010 grand final was drawn and replayed a week later; extra time for grand finals came in from 2016.
game_hook: A drawn grand final before 2016 means a replay week: fatigue and injury choices.

title: Seaford and back
summary: St Kilda moved its base to Seaford in 2010 and later returned to Moorabbin (year UNCERTAIN, about 2018).
game_hook: Training-base choice: new facilities versus the club's heartland.

title: Gold Coast Suns join
summary: The Gold Coast Suns entered the AFL in 2011 with list concessions.
game_hook: New rival with concessions bids for your players.

title: The green vest
summary: From 2011 to 2015 teams had three interchange players and one substitute; the sub was dropped in 2016.
game_hook: Rule-era flag: bench of 3 plus sub.

title: Betting on a teammate
summary: A Collingwood defender put $10 into a $20 bet on his captain kicking the first goal; the captain had told family about his forward role and they bet too.
penalty_or_outcome: Player banned 14 matches (6 suspended, 8 served) and fined $20,000; captain fined $5,000 plus $5,000 suspended.
game_hook: Team-news leak: coach decides how tightly to hold selections; a leak means suspensions mid-season.

title: The coach walks out
summary: St Kilda's coach used a get-out clause to sign with Fremantle in September 2011; Fremantle sacked its own coach the same night and paid out his contract.
game_hook: A rival club approaches your coach (or you): loyalty, board and press.

title: The secret trade guarantee
summary: Adelaide had a secret agreement guaranteeing a player a trade to a club of his choice plus an extra payment; it surfaced in 2012.
penalty_or_outcome: Club fined $300,000 and barred from the first two rounds of the 2013 draft (it had already handed back its first two 2012 picks); player banned 11 matches and fined $50,000; CEO suspended (6 months reported; club says 12 with half deferred); football manager 2 months.
game_hook: Agent asks for a secret side deal to re-sign a star: accept (risk picks) or refuse (he may walk).

title: GWS Giants join
summary: GWS entered the AFL in 2012 with list concessions.
game_hook: New rival with concessions; uncontracted players get big offers.

title: North goes to Hobart
summary: North Melbourne began taking home games to Hobart's Bellerive Oval from 2012 (year as commonly given; not checked).
game_hook: Sold home games: money versus home advantage.

title: Coach sacked for a premiership coach
summary: Carlton sacked its coach with a year to run in 2012 and hired a three-time premiership coach.
game_hook: Board flirts with a big-name coach while you are contracted.

title: The tanking inquiry
summary: An AFL inquiry into Melbourne's 2009 season, when it secured a priority pick, found the club not guilty of tanking but punished officials over their comments and conduct.
penalty_or_outcome: $500,000 fine; former coach suspended for the first 16 rounds of 2013; former football manager suspended until 1 February 2014.
game_hook: Late-season choice: rest stars and blood kids for a better pick (inquiry risk) or play to win.

title: The supplements saga
summary: Essendon's 2012 supplements program led to AFL charges in 2013 and an anti-doping case; in January 2016 CAS found 34 past and present players guilty of using a banned peptide.
penalty_or_outcome: 2013: $2m fine, thrown out of the finals (deemed ninth), early picks lost in 2013 and 2014 (detail varies), coach banned 12 months, football manager 6 months (2 suspended), assistant fined $30,000. 2016: 34 players banned two years backdated; 12 still at the club missed the whole 2016 season.
game_hook: Sports-science pitch: a bold program promising fitness gains versus compliance risk; if taken, years later the club loses finals, picks and half its list.

title: Abuse at the MCG
summary: In 2013 Sydney's Indigenous captain was racially abused by a young Collingwood supporter; days later Collingwood's president made a racially charged radio remark about him and apologised.
penalty_or_outcome: Supporter removed; apology; no AFL sanction found.
game_hook: Press: coach's response moves his player's morale and the club's standing.

title: Back to Adelaide Oval
summary: Both South Australian clubs moved their home games from Football Park to the redeveloped Adelaide Oval in 2014.
game_hook: Ground-move news story; gate money rises.

title: The trade ban
summary: After Sydney signed two marquee players, the AFL ruled in October 2014 that the Swans could not trade players in for two years unless they gave up their cost-of-living allowance.
penalty_or_outcome: Trade ban, later eased to players paid above the average wage.
game_hook: A big free-agent signing triggers league scrutiny: star in, trades frozen.

clubs: Sydney; Greater Western Sydney; Brisbane; Gold Coast
title: Academy bidding
summary: Northern academies handed top talent to Sydney cheaply in the 2014 draft, and a points-based bidding system for academy and father-son picks followed.
game_hook: Draft-rule event: northern clubs pay more for academy picks.

title: The booing
summary: Sustained booing of Sydney's Indigenous champion through 2015 led him to take leave from the game.
game_hook: Opposition crowds target your player: coach speaks out (press, morale) or stays quiet.

title: Coach sacked mid-season
summary: Carlton sacked its veteran premiership coach early in 2015 (round UNCERTAIN).
game_hook: Board patience event.

title: Interchange caps
summary: Interchange rotations were capped from 2014 and cut to 90 a game in 2016, when the sub was also dropped.
game_hook: Rule-era flag: fatigue matters more.

title: The veterans cull
summary: North Melbourne told several veterans, including its games-record holder, during the 2016 season that they would not get new contracts.
game_hook: List decision: cut beloved veterans (members angry) or keep them (slower rebuild).

title: Pay deal standoff
summary: Players pushed for a fixed share of league revenue; after eight months without a deal and talk of a pre-season strike, a six-year deal gave them 28 per cent of agreed revenue plus a share of windfalls.
game_hook: Players threaten to sit out pre-season games; coach's public stance moves morale versus board.

title: AFLW begins
summary: The AFL Women's competition launched in 2017.
game_hook: News story (flavour).

clubs: Port Adelaide; Gold Coast; St Kilda
title: Footy in Shanghai
summary: Port Adelaide played home games in Shanghai from 2017 to 2019 (Gold Coast in 2017, St Kilda in later years); the 2020 game was cancelled by COVID.
game_hook: Board sells a home game overseas: money versus travel.

title: Perth Stadium opens
summary: West Coast and Fremantle moved from Subiaco to the new Perth Stadium in 2018.
game_hook: Ground-move news story.

title: Etihad becomes Marvel Stadium
summary: The Docklands stadium was renamed Marvel Stadium in 2018.
game_hook: Short news story.

title: The pre-season camp
summary: Adelaide's 2018 pre-season camp, run by a mind-training company, left players distressed; the club cut ties mid-season and slid from grand finalist to 12th. Indigenous players later described it as harmful.
penalty_or_outcome: SafeWork SA found no breach in 2021; the club later apologised.
game_hook: After a grand final loss, the board pitches a radical team-bonding camp: possible cohesion gain versus a morale crash.

summary: Starting positions (six forwards, six mids, six backs at centre bounces) came in for 2019 to cut congestion.
game_hook: Rule-era flag.

title: Coach and CEO sacked
summary: Fremantle sacked its senior coach and its CEO together in August 2019.
game_hook: Board clean-out event.

title: The hub season
summary: The 2020 season was suspended after round 1, resumed on 11 June with shortened quarters, moved most clubs into Queensland hubs and ended with the first grand final outside Victoria, a night game at the Gabba.
penalty_or_outcome: Shortened 17-round season; pay and staff cuts across clubs (scale UNCERTAIN).
game_hook: Hub decisions: families in or out (morale); list and pay cuts (board, money).

title: The prison bars
summary: Port Adelaide was allowed one prison-bars match in 2020 for its 150th year, but the AFL refused in 2021 after Collingwood objected; Port changed into it after the Showdown to sing the song.
penalty_or_outcome: Port's chairman said the club faced a fine and lost points if it played in it without consent.
game_hook: Look never touches the sim: only press, board and members react.

title: Do Better
summary: An independent review found systemic racism at Collingwood; the president's reaction drew backlash and he resigned on 9 February 2021.
game_hook: Board review: coach backs reform (Indigenous players' morale up, some board friction) or deflects (press hit).

title: Grand final in Perth
summary: Victoria's lockdown moved the 2021 grand final to Perth Stadium.
game_hook: News story; neutral venue for the decider.

title: Medical sub and the stand rule
summary: 2021 brought a medical-only substitute (a subbed player out for 12 days) and the 'stand' rule for the man on the mark.
game_hook: Rule-era flag.

title: Coach steps down mid-season
summary: Collingwood's coach of ten seasons stepped down mid-2021.
game_hook: Board patience event.

title: The First Nations review
summary: A 2022 cultural safety review aired allegations of mistreatment of First Nations players and families; an AFL investigation ended in 2023 with no adverse findings against the officials named, and a Federal Court case settled in November 2024 with a club apology.
game_hook: Board commissions a review of the club's past: honesty costs short-term press, avoidance risks a worse story later.

title: White powder photo
summary: A Bulldogs player was suspended after images circulated of him with a white powder.
game_hook: Player conduct: coach backs him publicly or distances the club.

title: Review and sacking
summary: Essendon commissioned an external review and sacked its coach in August 2022.
game_hook: Board review event.

title: CEO gone in a day
summary: Essendon's new CEO resigned a day after his appointment in October 2022 when his role as chair of a church with views on abortion and homosexuality caused backlash; the club apologised to him in December.
game_hook: Board appointment backfires: press and members turn; coach asked to comment.

title: First joint AFL-AFLW pay deal
summary: A five-year collective agreement covering both AFL and AFLW players for 2023-2027 was signed after drawn-out talks (dispute details not checked).
game_hook: Cap rises; flavour news.

title: The 19th licence
summary: Tasmania was granted the 19th licence in May 2023 on condition of a roofed Hobart stadium; the fight over the stadium ran through 2025, the venue is not expected until 2031, and the club still targets 2028 entry.
game_hook: Future rival: Tasmanian-born players may want to go home; Tasmanian games sold by other clubs end.

title: Triple premiership coach quits
summary: Richmond's three-time premiership coach resigned in May 2023.
game_hook: Coach burnout event (if the player is the coach: a wellbeing gate).

title: Gather Round
summary: From 2023 every club played one round in South Australia, costing some clubs a home game.
game_hook: Home game lost to a neutral round: money from the league versus home advantage.

title: The concussion class action
summary: In March 2023 a former Geelong premiership player led a Supreme Court class action for players concussed since 1985; Geelong was added in 2024, over 100 players had joined by March 2026, and part of the claim was dismissed in early 2026.
penalty_or_outcome: Ongoing; no settlement found; damages sought near $1 billion.
game_hook: Coach decisions on rushing concussed players back can surface years later as board and legal costs.

title: Trafficking ban
summary: A Melbourne player tested positive for cocaine in 2023 and was found to have trafficked it; the club denied a drug culture.
penalty_or_outcome: Banned four years and three months, to 9 January 2028.
game_hook: Press asks about club culture; coach defends or orders a review.

title: Secret testing allegations
summary: In March 2024 an MP alleged under parliamentary privilege that the AFL ran off-the-books illicit drug tests and had players fake injuries to hide positives.
penalty_or_outcome: League denied hiding results; in 2026 an in-principle new policy ended three strikes (2-4 match bans for public use, six-monthly hair tests).
game_hook: Press asks whether your 'injured' players were really injured.

clubs: Port Adelaide; Gold Coast; St Kilda; North Melbourne; West Coast; Adelaide; Sydney; Brisbane
title: Homophobic slur bans
summary: From 2024 the AFL banned a string of players for homophobic slurs.
penalty_or_outcome: Bans of 3, 4, 5 and 6 matches; one sent a player out of the 2025 finals; a coach fined $20,000 with a suspended two-match ban.
game_hook: Your player is reported for a slur: self-report (shorter ban) or contest.

title: The costume party
summary: GWS players dressed in a 'controversial couples' theme at a September 2024 end-of-season function; an anonymous complaint led to conduct-unbecoming charges.
penalty_or_outcome: Six players suspended (one 4 matches, the rest 2), seven fined.
game_hook: Coach sets end-of-season standards: weak rules risk round 1 suspensions.

title: Coach out mid-season
summary: West Coast and its premiership coach parted ways after round 17 of 2024.
game_hook: Board patience event.

title: Premiership coach sacked
summary: Melbourne sacked its 2021 premiership coach on 5 August 2025 with three rounds left, after a 7-13 season.
game_hook: Board patience event even for a premiership coach.

title: Hotel incident stand-downs
summary: After an August 2026 incident at a Melbourne team hotel, under police investigation with no charges laid as of late August, Sydney stood five players down for the rest of the season including finals for breaching club standards.
penalty_or_outcome: Five players out; sponsors paused deals; Prime Minister criticised the AFL. ONGOING and SENSITIVE (alleged sexual assault).
game_hook: Standards call before finals: stand players down (weaker side, board and press respect) or keep them (press, sponsors). Director should rule on inclusion.

title: Three strikes scrapped
summary: The AFL and players agreed in principle in 2026 to replace the three-strikes illicit drugs policy with match bans for public use and regular hair testing.
game_hook: League rule event.
